context_requirements: Human cells do not express bacterial beta-lactamases or penicillin-binding proteins, so the drug class has no canonical target in these lines
A response would require an off-target activity (e.g. serine protease or host enzyme inhibition) that is not established for this class
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines
Shared transcriptional signature across lines that is not explained by vehicle or general cytotoxicity
Evidence of a specific off-target pathway (e.g. ER stress, protease inhibition) responding consistently

changes: Removed PMID 40422913 from evidence: its abstract concerns clavulanic acid production in Streptomyces clavuligerus, not a transcriptional response to a beta-lactamase inhibitor in human cell lines, so it does not support any claim in this hypothesis.
